newsitem.title: USA: U.S. industry quick to slam EPA air proposal.
newsitem.headline: U.S. industry quick to slam EPA air proposal.

text.p: U.S. industry groups instantly protested a proposal that the Environmental Protection Agency unveiled on Wednesday to tighten air quality standards.

The National Association of Manufacturers said the proposal to toughen limits on smog and fine particles from smokestacks would "double or triple" the number of counties that failed to meet air quality standards and choke business.

"The restrictions the new, more stringent standards will have on business expansion and start-up will have a chilling effect on economic growth in this country," said Owen Drey of the National Association of Manufacturers.
The National Association of Manufacturers, which is leading industry's fight against higher standards, said it would be premature to require more rigid air quality controls.
The American Trucking Associations said the new the standards would "cost consumers billions of dollars, destory jobs and potentially disrupt the movement of goods and supplies around the nation."
Health advocates urged EPA to stand up to business groups in what is expected to be a major battle before the agency issues a final rule next year.

"We urge the Clinton Administration to ignore the special interests, and go even further than today's proposal to fully protect the public from the dangers of air pollution," said the U.S. Public Interest Research Group.
